ai.description: The Kempholey toad reaches 4–5 cm. It is dark brown with a pale mid-dorsal stripe and granular skin. Key features include a short, blunt snout and prominent, kidney-shaped parotoid glands.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Kempholey Toad is best distinguished by its distinct, thickened, and glandular skin folds that form a prominent, continuous ridge extending from behind the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: The Kempholey Toad inhabits the leaf litter of evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kempholey toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates along the forest floor of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Kempholey toad breeds in seasonal streams during the monsoon (June–August). They are oviparous, laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kempholey toad is endemic to the central Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kempholey Toad produces a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard while calling from leaf litter in moist evergreen forests.
